subject: SOC 2 coverage: routing fallback impact for Dedicated->Hosted paths
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@bluepeak.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 question — Dedicated pool + occasional hosted fallback

Hi Markus,

Quick follow-up from our security review: BluePeak intends to run production traffic on a Dedicated pool in our AWS account, but we understand Redwood’s routing policy allows bursts to overflow to your hosted runtime in some cases (burst capacity, model variant availability, or maintenance windows).

Can you confirm whether the hosted runtime that a request may be routed to will be covered by Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II for the same audit period (2026 Type II)? If not, what evidence or mitigations are available so BluePeak can present a contiguous control narrative to our auditors?

Specifically we need:
- A copy (redacted ok) of the SOC 2 Type II report that covers hosted inference used for routing fallbacks.
- Whether you can produce a short written attestation / bridge letter that states the hosted fallback was included in scope for the audit period (or clearly call out the exception).
- A list of configuration items and logs we should capture to demonstrate tenant isolation when fallback happens (routing decision logs, tenant mapping, request traces, timestamps).

We’re trying to avoid raising a finding; if you can point to the minimum evidence to assemble a packaging we’ll share with our auditors that would be great.

Thanks — happy to hop on a brief call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Security Manager, BluePeak Financial

Attachments referenced: none in this message

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 question — Dedicated pool + occasional hosted fallback

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list.

Short answer: we can support BluePeak here, but there are conditionals we should document so your auditors can follow the control boundary. High-level:
- Dedicated pools are tenant-isolated and in-scope for customer-specific commitments when customers purchase Dedicated.
- Our hosted runtime (the fallback target) is a separate infrastructure layer that is in-scope for Redwood’s 2026 SOC 2 Type II report, but the applicability depends on whether customer data is processed there during the audit period.

I’m attaching a redacted copy of our 2026 SOC 2 Type II report and a draft bridge-letter template we typically use for hybrid cases (attached).

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi — can you confirm the minimal evidence items we should provide for the fallback path (routing decision logs, tenant map exports, and any config snapshots)?
2) Sarah — if BluePeak has a specific auditor contact or a scope definition we should align to, please share.

I’ve attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_report_redacted.pdf and bridge-letter-dedicated-to-hosted-template.docx. I also included a short workbook listing the likely evidence artifacts (request_evidence_inventory.xlsx).

We can also prepare a signed bridge letter once Rishi confirms the phrasing.

Best,
Markus
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_report_redacted.pdf (redacted), bridge-letter-dedicated-to-hosted-template.docx, request_evidence_inventory.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 question — Dedicated pool + occasional hosted fallback

Rishi — forwarding BluePeak’s note and Markus’s attachments. Please see the ask bullets below (copied):

- Confirm whether hosted fallback processing is captured by the 2026 SOC 2 Type II report (and if so, what page/section evidences it).
- Provide a concise list of evidence artifacts BluePeak should include with auditor submission: routing decision logs, tenant mapping exports, KV cache/TTL config, any isolation test results, and change-control records for routing policies.
- Suggested bridge-letter wording: does the template cover the burst/fallback case or do we need to call out exception windows?
- Sampling guidance: auditors will ask whether event sampling could miss fallback cases — do we have an approach to show sampling covers fallback events during the audit window?

Notes: BluePeak wants the smallest possible package to avoid a long rework with their procurement/audit teams. If we can provide a short checklist + signed bridge letter, that’ll likely close it.

Can you reply with suggested wording we can send to Sarah and any redaction guidance for the report?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Sr. Security Programs Manager (Sales Enablement)
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@bluepeak.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 question — Dedicated pool + occasional hosted fallback

Hi Sarah and Markus — sorry for the delay, wanted to validate with controls and infra teams. Summary below and proposed next steps.

Summary of coverage
- Hosted fallback runtime was evaluated during Redwood’s 2026 Type II engagement. The control testing included the hosted inference cluster used in production (see redacted report section summary attached). That means the hosted runtime is part of Redwood’s SOC 2 boundary for the 2026 period.
- That said, to link BluePeak’s Dedicated-to-hosted fallback events to that coverage we need event-level evidence showing when a request actually traversed the hosted path. Presence of the hosted runtime in our SOC 2 boundary alone is insufficient for an auditor to conclude BluePeak’s specific requests were inside scope without those traces.

Minimum evidence checklist (we can produce these items)
- Routing decision log extract (time-windowed): timestamp, request id, originating Dedicated pool id, decision reason (burst/variant-unavailable), target runtime id.
- Tenant mapping export for the relevant timeframe: customer id -> pool id / runtime id mapping.
- Config snapshot for routing policy active during audit window (hash + human-readable).
- Change-control record showing no unauthorized routing rule changes in period (PR/approval links).
- Sampled request traces (3–5 examples) that show a full request lifecycle across Dedicated->Hosted transition (redacted tokens/inputs as needed).

Bridge letter guidance
- The bridge letter should state: (a) the hosted runtime was included in Redwood’s 2026 SOC 2 Type II audit boundary, (b) when BluePeak requests were processed by the hosted runtime during the audit period, the processing occurred on that in-scope infrastructure, and (c) provide a short caveat about the auditor needing request-level logs to validate specific events.
- I’ve attached a filled draft (bridge-letter-dedicated-to-hosted-template.docx) with suggested wording; we will sign and return via DocuSign.

Next steps and timelines
1) Markus/Kim: confirm BluePeak’s desired audit window (they requested calendar-year 2026 coverage).
2) BluePeak (Sarah): confirm 72-hour retrieval windows you need for the evidence. We can produce extracts for a rolling 90-day period by standard process; for older windows we’ll need a slightly longer lead time.
3) We will send the signed bridge letter via DocuSign and upload the redacted report to the secure portal.

DocuSign link (for bridge letter): https://docusign.com/link/REDWOOD-BRIDGE-1892
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/deals/BLUEPEAK-1892

If you’d like, we can run a 30-min walkthrough with your auditors to walk through the artifacts.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: bridge-letter-dedicated-to-hosted-template.docx (draft — not yet signed), Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_report_redacted.pdf (as shared earlier), request_evidence_inventory.xlsx
